Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

depend verb

rely on

also depend on, rely on, count on, you can count on me, dependent, rely

classical

Cic. Off. 1.122: quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur
Traupman 96, 297: potes nītī mē, you can count on me

nītor, nītī, nīsus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent: with the ablative, or in and the ablative

rely on, rest on, lean on

Properly “lean on, press against”, then “rely on” whatever holds one up: spē nītī (Cic. Att. 3.9.2, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short give the perfect as nīsus or nixus. To depend on someone for one’s keep is to be fed by them: Ā parentibus adhūc alitur, he still depends on his parents (M-O s.v. support: dependent).

Examples

  • Est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī exque iīs dēligere optimōs et probātissimōs, quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur

    It is a young man’s part, then, to respect his elders and to choose from among them the best and most approved, on whose advice and authority he can relyCic. Off. 1.122

  • quō cōnfugiēs? ubi nītēre?

    where will you run to? what will you rely on?Cic. Verr. 2.2.155

  • nam omnēs mortālēs dīs sunt frētī, sed tamen vīdī ego dīs frētōs saepe multōs dēcipī

    for all men rely on the gods; and yet I have often seen many who relied on the gods let downPlaut. Cas. 348–349

Other words

  • cōnfīdō, cōnfīdere, cōnfīsus sum — trust, rely on

    verb, third conjugation, semi-deponent: with the dative of a person, the ablative of a thing · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 8.13.2: illum, quō anteā cōnfīdēbant, metuunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 157, 370

  • frētus, frēta, frētum — relying on, trusting in

    adjective, with the ablative · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 348: omnēs mortālēs dīs sunt frētī; Cic. Planc. 103: vōbīs frētus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 157, 370

See also depend, faith, help.
